text:
[IARC.2.3] **No protocol, no peer, no wire.** Every interaction
that crosses libds's boundary — telemetry emission, action
dispatch, fact assertion from outside, debug subscription —
goes through a typed callback the integrator registers. libds
defines the *shape of the data* that crosses (struct layouts,
event payloads, opaque handles); it never defines bytes,
framing, or transport. Cross-process or cross-machine concerns
(e.g., bridging two libds instances, network-attached storage,
remote debugging) are entirely the integrator's responsibility.
See [IARC.1.14] for the load-bearing invariant; this module
graph reflects it.
